_readme: Quality ratchet: these numbers are the worst accepted state. A PR may add code but may not worsen any metric - not even by one unit. Re-freezing is deliberate (`pnpm quality --update-baseline`) and the reason goes in the commit body; this file is versioned precisely so the change shows in the diff.
_mode: Every metric here uses "baseline" (freeze today's value, only allow improvement) - the mode for a repo with existing debt. A fresh repo may prefer "floor" with explicit thresholds; see compare.mts.

cobertura-percentual.label: Cobertura de linhas
cobertura-percentual.note: Covered lines / instrumented lines over the wide slice (vitest.quality.config.ts). Catches dilution; the per-file ratchet catches local regressions.

linhas-descobertas.label: Linhas descobertas
linhas-descobertas.note: Informative only - the per-file ratchet (uncoveredByFile) is what fails the build.

duplicacao-percentual.label: Linhas duplicadas
duplicacao-percentual.note: jscpd over src/. An agent edits one copy and misses the others - duplication is refactor risk, not aesthetics.

regra-pura-fora-do-dominio.label: Regra pura fora do domínio
regra-pura-fora-do-dominio.note: A .ts outside the rule directories WITH a unit test beside it - the signature of a business rule born at the edge. Complements the import-direction lint, which cannot see a rule that never reached domain/.

arquivos-acima-do-limite.label: Arquivos acima do limite
arquivos-acima-do-limite.note: Production files over LIMITE_DE_LINHAS (size.mts). Big files are where the next agent edit turns into a mess.

any-explicito.label: `any` explícito
any-explicito.note: AST count of `any` keyword nodes in production files (any-count.mts). AGENTS.md bans new `any`; the ratchet lets legacy debt only shrink. Exists because flipping no-explicit-any to 'error' over legacy code breaks the build on day one.
